triple.variant_context: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations or homozygous deletion of SMN1 gene; SMN2 exon 7 splice silencer ISS-N1 targeted by the ASO
triple.molecular_target: SMN2 pre-mRNA intron 7 intronic splicing silencer ISS-N1 (no UniProt; RNA target)
triple.mechanism_summary: Nusinersen is a 2'-O-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide that base-pairs with the intronic splicing silencer ISS-N1 in SMN2 intron 7, blocking hnRNP A1/A2 binding and thereby promoting exon 7 inclusion, which increases production of full-length, functional SMN protein in motor neurons.

triple.indicated_disease: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) with biallelic SMN1 mutations in patients <2 years
triple.variant_context: Biallelic SMN1 deletion or loss-of-function mutations causing absence of functional SMN protein; single-dose gene replacement regardless of SMN2 copy number
triple.molecular_target: SMN1 locus (transgene delivered via AAV9 capsid; no UniProt target — gene addition therapy)
triple.mechanism_summary: Onasemnogene abeparvovec is an AAV9 vector carrying a self-complementary DNA construct encoding functional human SMN1 under a cytomegalovirus-enhanced chicken beta-actin promoter, enabling stable, long-term SMN protein expression in motor neurons following a single intravenous dose.

discrepancies: ChEMBL does not carry a dedicated entry for gene therapies; validation performed via DrugBank DB15779 only

triple.indicated_disease: Cystic fibrosis (CF) with CFTR gating mutations (G551D and other class III/IV variants)
triple.variant_context: G551D (c.1652G>A, p.Gly551Asp) gating mutation in CFTR and ≥11 other gating or residual-function mutations; not effective for F508del homozygous patients alone
triple.molecular_target: P13569 (CFTR) — ATP-binding cassette transporter subfamily C member 7
triple.mechanism_summary: Ivacaftor is a CFTR channel potentiator that binds to the membrane-spanning domains of CFTR and increases the open-channel probability of the defective protein, restoring chloride ion transport at the epithelial surface without correcting protein folding.

triple.indicated_disease: Fabry disease with amenable GLA variants
triple.variant_context: GLA missense variants amenable to pharmacological chaperone rescue (approximately 35–50% of known pathogenic variants); NOT effective for null variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site loss-of-function)
triple.mechanism_summary: Migalastat is an iminosugar pharmacological chaperone that binds the active site of misfolded, amenable alpha-galactosidase A (GLA) variants in the endoplasmic reticulum, stabilizing the enzyme and improving its trafficking to the lysosome where it reduces globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation.

discrepancies: DrugBank lists mechanism as 'pharmacological chaperone / enzyme stabilizer'; ChEMBL lists as 'positive allosteric modulator'; both are consistent with the active-site chaperone classification used here

triple.indicated_disease: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS) and processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies
triple.variant_context: De novo LMNA c.1824C>T (p.G608G) splice-site mutation producing progerin (truncated lamin A with 50-aa internal deletion near C-terminus); also for ZMPSTE24 processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies
triple.molecular_target: Q14192 (FNTB) — farnesyltransferase subunit beta; prevents farnesylation of progerin C-terminal CAAX motif
triple.mechanism_summary: Lonafarnib inhibits protein farnesyltransferase, blocking the first step of post-translational CAAX-motif processing of progerin. Without farnesylation, progerin accumulates less efficiently in the inner nuclear membrane, reducing nuclear envelope dysfunction and extending organismal lifespan.

triple.indicated_disease: Hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR) with polyneuropathy in adults
triple.variant_context: TTR pathogenic variants (including V30M, V122I, T60A, and >100 others) causing misfolded transthyretin tetramer destabilization and amyloid fibril deposition; efficacy also demonstrated in wild-type TTR amyloidosis (ATTRwt)
triple.molecular_target: P02766 (TTR) — transthyretin mRNA (hepatic); drug reduces circulating TTR protein
triple.mechanism_summary: Vutrisiran is a GalNAc3-conjugated siRNA that is selectively taken up by hepatocytes via ASGR1 and directs RISC-mediated cleavage of TTR mRNA, reducing hepatic synthesis of all TTR protein variants by >80% and thereby preventing amyloid precursor supply.

discrepancies: PMID 35658024 (Adams D et al, NEJM 2022 HELIOS-A trial) is the registrational trial basis; PMID requires final librarian verification — number sourced from NLM PubMed 2025-01-15

triple.indicated_disease: Acute hepatic porphyria (AHP), including acute intermittent porphyria (AIP), hereditary coproporphyria (HCP), variegate porphyria (VP)
triple.variant_context: Loss-of-function mutations in HMBS (AIP), CPOX (HCP), or PPOX (VP) causing derepression of ALAS1 and toxic porphyrin precursor accumulation; drug targets downstream ALAS1 regardless of upstream variant
triple.mechanism_summary: Givosiran is a GalNAc3-conjugated siRNA that silences hepatic ALAS1 mRNA via RISC-mediated cleavage, reducing ALA and PBG synthesis and preventing accumulation of neurotoxic porphyrin precursors that trigger acute attacks.

triple.indicated_disease: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), types 1–3 and presymptomatic
triple.variant_context: Biallelic SMN1 loss-of-function with residual SMN2 copies; oral small-molecule alternative to ASO nusinersen; effective across all SMA types and ages
triple.molecular_target: SMN2 pre-mRNA — drug stabilises the 5' splice site of exon 7 by interacting with U1-snRNP and SRSF1 splicing factors (RNA target, no UniProt accession)
triple.mechanism_summary: Risdiplam is an orally bioavailable pyridazine that penetrates the CNS and acts on SMN2 pre-mRNA splicing by stabilising the U1-snRNP interaction at the exon 7 5'-splice site and modulating SRSF1 binding, thereby increasing exon 7 inclusion and full-length SMN protein production in both peripheral and CNS tissues.

discrepancies: Mechanism class listed as 'modulator' here (SMN2 splicing modifier); ChEMBL lists 'RNA binding protein modulator' — consistent with our classification

triple.indicated_disease: Sickle cell disease (SCD) in patients ≥12 years; transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia (TDT, approved 2024-01-16)
triple.variant_context: SCD: HBB c.20A>T (p.Glu7Val, rs334) homozygous or compound heterozygous; TDT: biallelic HBB loss-of-function. CRISPR edit targets BCL11A erythroid-specific enhancer (GATA1-bound +58 region), not HBB directly
triple.molecular_target: BCL11A erythroid enhancer (chr2:60,495,250-60,495,390 hg38) — transcriptional repressor of fetal hemoglobin (no UniProt; regulatory DNA target)
triple.mechanism_summary: Exagamglogene autotemcel uses CRISPR-Cas9 to disrupt the GATA1-binding erythroid enhancer of BCL11A in autologous CD34+ HSCs, eliminating BCL11A expression in erythroid progenitors and derepressing gamma-globin (HBG1/HBG2) synthesis, which reactivates fetal hemoglobin (HbF) to levels sufficient to prevent sickling and reduce transfusion dependence.

discrepancies: ChEMBL and DrugBank do not yet carry this approval; validated against FDA press release, CLIMB-SCD-121 trial (NCT03745287), and NEJM publication PMID 37542486. PMID requires final librarian verification.

triple.indicated_disease: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) requiring additional LDL-C lowering
triple.variant_context: HeFH caused by LDLR, APOB, or PCSK9 gain-of-function variants; inclisiran acts downstream of the causal variant by silencing hepatic PCSK9 regardless of upstream genotype
triple.molecular_target: P53779 (PCSK9) — proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 mRNA (hepatic); GalNAc-conjugate delivered to hepatocytes via ASGR1
triple.mechanism_summary: Inclisiran is a GalNAc3-conjugated synthetic double-stranded siRNA that is taken up by hepatocytes via asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGR1) and directs RISC-mediated cleavage of PCSK9 mRNA, reducing PCSK9 protein secretion, increasing hepatic LDL receptor recycling, and lowering circulating LDL-C by approximately 50% with twice-yearly subcutaneous dosing.
